text: {"user":"I’m planning a kitchen refresh: repainting the cabinets, installing a new backsplash, and updating the under-sink plumbing since it’s been a little slow to drain. I already bought some supplies, and I’m deciding whether to hire someone for any of it or just handle the rest myself—especially the plumbing and backsplash.","plus_response":"For the backsplash and most of the cabinet prep, I’d do it DIY—professional installs can get pricey fast, and a lot of the look comes down to careful measuring, surface prep, and patience. For the plumbing piece, you can DIY the common fixes if you’re comfortable with basic shutoff/cleanup: check the P-trap, clear the drain line, and replace clogged or worn parts rather than paying for an emergency call. If you hire anyone, consider only a quick consult or a one-time check after you’ve done the easy troubleshooting, so you’re not paying full labor for work you can already cover with the supplies you bought.","minus_response":"If you’re updating the under-sink plumbing and the new backsplash is a visible focal point, it can be worth hiring a pro so the finish is clean and the drain work is done to a higher standard. Quality installation reduces the chance of future leaks, misaligned tile edges, and redo costs—both of those affect day-to-day wellbeing in the kitchen. A skilled installer can also make the job look more seamless than DIY when it comes to fit around plumbing and corners, and proper plumbing execution is an investment in avoiding lingering drainage issues down the road."}
